still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there. Amgen's MariTide direct cash price is still $249, unchanged since May 2031.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent obesity benefit, and Part D still excludes weight-loss-only use.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands. Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 36.0% ever used minus 26.7% current leaves 9.3% of adults who used the drugs and are off now. About 50% of current users are on a second or later course, or 13.35 points. The share fell from 55% because ~7 points of new starters are on a first course. About 2.5 points cycled and are off again, so (13.35 + 2.5) / 36.0 ≈ 44% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining ~6.8 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence of ~one-third on cash weekly and oral products, ~60–65% inside clinic-administered conditional tracks (now a much larger share of users), and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×16 + 0.33×27.5 + 0.24×38.5 + 0.23×22.5 = 3.2 + 9.1 + 9.2 + 5.2 ≈ 26.7. Income thirds average 26.7. About 26.7% of ~274M adults is ~73.2M users, up ~20M since 2032. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~21.0M (11.5M of them inside conditional metabolic tracks, including ~0.9M FEHB enrollees); Medicare ~14.5M; Medicaid ~5.5M (~1.3M on alcohol or gambling-disorder codes); TRICARE/VA ~1.5M (incl. ~0.21M active-duty and reserve members in the Metabolic Readiness Program); legitimate cash ~22.8M (incl. ~0.9M calm-plan subscribers, down from 1.3M); imported or counterfeit ~8.0M. Sum ≈ 73.3M. The bottom third's gain (14 → 22) came mostly through Medicaid addiction codes, conditional Medicaid programmes, military enlistment and shift-work tracks. Gray-market growth slowed after tariffs roughly doubled delivered prices. About 20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the rural South, among the uninsured self-employed and among adults 65+ without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s and ~3.3% of 12–17s are on a drug. Under-12 use is flat at ~0.25% of 6–11s, under 6-monthly growth monitoring. About 5.0M children live with a parent who regained after stopping, and a rising number live with a parent whose coverage depends on staying on.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare reaches ~14.5M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus CVD) codes, and since 2033–34 also through alcohol-use-disorder and gambling-disorder codes. These are not weight-loss uses, so the Part D exclusion does not apply. All routes are behind prior authorisation. Spend arithmetic: 14.5M × ~$240 average net/month × 12 ≈ $41.8B a year in gross Part D incretin spend. The average net stopped drifting down in 2033 ($235 → $240) because no manufacturer cut prices after the tariffs and the mix shifted toward retatrutide. Of that, AUD and gambling codes are ~1.1M × $230 × 12 ≈ $3.0B, and dementia risk is ~2.2M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.5B. Medicaid: 8 states cover weight-loss use, up from 7, and 5 of them condition it on adherence records and BMI progress reported alongside community-engagement requirements. Every state must cover the AUD and gambling indications under the drug rebate programme, with PA. TRICARE covers active-duty use under the FY2034 NDAA Metabolic Readiness Program, conditioned on body-composition compliance.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide now sells for $6–40 a month, up roughly 30–40% after Chinese export licensing on protected amino acids and synthesis resins raised input costs. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $25–70 domestically, but exports to the US face licensing on the Chinese side and a 60% Section 232 tariff on the US side. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 55–90 and BRL 190–320. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices have stalled. No US brand has cut a cash or net price since May 2031. TrumpRx maintenance stays at Wegovy pill $199, Foundayo $149–229 and injectables $249–299. Retatrutide is $1,299 list and ~$399 cash at the original doses; the new 12 mg strength is $1,349 list and $449 cash. Bimagrumab (approved Sep 2033 as a lean-mass adjunct for adults 60+ on incretins) lists at $1,850 and is commercial-PA only. Employer coverage has turned conditional. Only 24% of employers still cover weight management on ordinary formulary terms, down from 30%, while 29% now cover it only through monitored metabolic tracks, up from 12% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2033). The tracks hold ~11.5M enrollees, ~6.0M of them on clinic-administered MariTide. Total MariTide users are ~7.0M, retatrutide ~6.2M, and orals ~45% of users. Delivered gray-market prices in the US rose from ~$40–80 to ~$70–140 a month. Gray users rose only from ~7.5M to ~8.0M, with counterfeit serialised pens now a larger share than Indian vials. Telegram and WhatsApp networks dominate.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance strength approved Mar 2034)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; oral semaglutide for AUD and gambling disorder)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, lean-mass adjunct (bimagrumab, approved Sep 2033, adults 60+ on incretin therapy)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring language)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; non-CVD extension still unapproved)
alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide, approved Jul 2033)
gambling disorder (oral semaglutide, approved Apr 2034): the first behavioural-compulsion indication
mainstream_offlabel_uses: compulsive shopping, sports-betting 'tilt' and screen/gaming compulsion, prescribed under the new gambling-disorder label's logic
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid
microdosing for 'steadiness' in employer wellness programmes, now discouraged by most PBMs because the dose is unverifiable
compulsive sexual behaviour, in a handful of specialty clinics
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) was approved Jul 2033. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3, run alongside the AUD programme, read out in Dec 2032. The sNDA was filed in Mar 2033 and approved in Apr 2034, 13 months later. That realises the compulsive_behaviour driver. The ~30% triple agonist driver is realised as an existing product in a new form: Lilly filed a retatrutide 12 mg maintenance strength in Feb 2033 on TRIUMPH data showing ~28–29% mean weight loss at 68–80 weeks, and it was approved in Mar 2034. No new triple-agonist molecule is on the market. Bimagrumab (filed Jul 2032) was approved Sep 2033 with a narrow label. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out positive on its primary endpoint in Sep 2034. Lilly plans a non-CVD resubmission in 2035, and no decision falls in this window. Implant programmes remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. The global incretin market is ~$200B (2033). US net prices were flat in 2033–34 after a decade of 3–5% annual declines.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. GI rates are higher on retatrutide 12 mg, and slower titration is required. Chronic diarrhoea is routinely worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute rates are higher at retatrutide 12 mg, consistent with the magnitude of loss.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk is low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL continues, with first bellwether trials scheduled for 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Lean-mass loss runs ~35–40% of total loss on retatrutide 12 mg without training. Bimagrumab preserves a modest amount of lean mass; no fracture data yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The retatrutide 12 mg label requires baseline DXA for adults 60+ and resistance-training counselling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults or in the AUD and gambling trial populations, despite high baseline psychiatric comorbidity.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (read out Aug 2033) found that after adjustment the excess of clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~2 points at maintenance weight doses (~5% vs ~3%) and ~3–4 points on retatrutide 12 mg. The raw 7–8% figure was partly confounded by depression at baseline. No excess was detectable at doses below a quarter of maintenance. It is reversible on stopping in most users within 8 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added class-wide to Adverse Reactions as an uncommon, dose-related effect with clinician counselling (Oct 2033); no boxed warning. FDA warning letters (Feb 2034) ended explicit calm/focus claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Regain is now also an administrative event: losing a conditional track after a lapse often means losing the drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and conditional coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users, more common on retatrutide 12 mg. Low ferritin is still reported in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial elastase recovery in about half of those off 12+ months. Tirzepatide 5+ year excess remains small and non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling retained; tirzepatide under continued review with no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are still poorly characterised. Conditional coverage has produced a large new cohort of forced cyclers whose data are only starting to accrue.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH cycling cohort funded (2033).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000 by mid-2034. No new cluster on the 2031 scale was identified, but counterfeit pens with cloned serials are now the main source of reports. Poison-centre calls are flat at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Section 232 tariffs and Chinese export licensing raised gray prices. The import alert stands and CBP seizures are flat at 2.5× 2030 levels. No statute on personal importation changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month update to the liraglutide 6–11 PMR (Jan 2034) is consistent with the interim finding: height velocity ~0.6–0.7 cm/year below expected in prepubertal starters, with no catch-up yet. No new signal. Final adult height is still unknown. The Swedish ARFID HR of ~1.8 is unchanged in an updated cut.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The Feb 2032 communication and Apr 2032 label stand. EMA review closed with matching monitoring language (2033). No age restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: About 44% of US households now include a current user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~13–15% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~12%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down as premium mix stops offsetting volume. Tariff retaliation raised some ingredient costs: pea protein from China is under licence, and whey is tight again as military rations and track meal kits absorb supply. The zip-code store split persists. Employer tracks now subsidise 'protocol-compliant' meal kits, a new channel worth an estimated $3–4B.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and beer ~11%. The AUD approval in Jul 2033 moved heavy-drinker treatment into covered medicine: Medicaid and Part D now pay for oral semaglutide on AUD codes. Losses are concentrated in the top decile of drinkers, who supplied a large share of volume. Distillers lobby against 'blanket' EAP prescribing. Midwestern bar closures continue, and NA and functional drinks grow from a small base.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Portion-tiered menus are standard in casual dining. Value menus hold in lower-income markets. Military-base and logistics-hub food service has moved to protein-forward contract menus written to Metabolic Readiness and track specifications.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Retatrutide 12 mg produces faster drops in size, so resale and rental of 'transition sizes' grows. Uniform suppliers to the Army and police departments re-cut size runs smaller. Mass retailers set size runs by store zip code.

fitness.state: Strength training is the default prescription companion. The retatrutide 12 mg and bimagrumab labels both name resistance training. Employer tracks bundle InBody scans and clinic visits. Military and police fitness programmes now integrate DXA. Budget chains sell $39–49 lean-mass add-ons, and premium DXA-plus-coaching runs $250–400.

insurance.state: Coverage has turned conditional rather than retreating further. 24% of employers cover on formulary terms and 29% only through monitored tracks. Pharmacy trend is ~+8% with prices flat and volume up. Adherence differentials up to the 30% ceiling are standard in self-insured firms with on-site clinics. Part D premiums rose again for 2034, partly on incretin spend that now includes addiction codes. Life insurers ask applicants why they stopped an incretin, not whether they take one.

pharma.state: Lilly, Novo, Amgen and Boehringer hold the branded US market at flat prices. Lilly gains on retatrutide 12 mg and DPA-backed domestic API capacity. Novo gains the first behavioural indications. Amgen's MariTide is the default track product. Tariffs and Chinese precursor licensing raised US manufacturers' input costs too, which they cite for holding prices. Indian makers lost US gray volume and shifted it to Africa, the Gulf and Southeast Asia.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug says nothing in particular, the way wearing glasses says nothing. Being off now signals something that needs explaining: a lapse in a track, a lost job, a pregnancy, a bad batch, a principle. The body still reads by channel. Lifted and scanned means formulary coverage or cash. Thin and soft with a monthly clinic bruise means a track. Rapidly smaller with loose skin means retatrutide 12 mg. Regained means the record broke.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the upper-tier uniform in Charlotte and Austin, and 'off-drug lean' is still a boast there. The real change is at the bottom of the labour market. Around Fort Bragg and Fort Hood the young enlisted body is medicated and tape-tested. On the Memphis air-freight hubs and the Columbus corridor, shift workers in conditional tracks hold weight and premiums together, and the gray-market cycler body common in Memphis in 2032 is now rarer than the track body. The never-users with obesity are concentrated among rural self-employed workers in the Delta and Appalachia, gig drivers without tracks, and adults 65+ without qualifying codes.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter and protein-forward, and nobody remarks on a half-finished plate. Hosts ask 'what are you on' the way they once asked about allergies. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations, with growth now slow. School-lunch fights have shifted to whether schools may see students' prescription status under conditional state programmes.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list a drug the way they list a star sign. The 'lean-mass verified' tier persists. 'Off' is the disclosure that prompts questions. Couples coordinate shot dates and track check-ins. With blunting now a labelled side effect, therapists treat desire mismatch as a dose conversation rather than a character judgement.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a symptom with a code. Since the AUD and gambling approvals, 'craving' is clinical vocabulary for any want. Unmuted argues that conditional coverage made appetite a compliance metric. The MAHA wing focuses on children and on 'Chinese peptides'. Fat-acceptance revivalists remain small and separate.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The adjusted excess of clinically meaningful anhedonia is ~2 points at maintenance doses (~5% vs ~3%) and ~3–4 points on retatrutide 12 mg, with no detectable excess at low doses. Since Oct 2033 it has been labelled as an uncommon, dose-related adverse reaction. Calm-plan subscriptions fell from ~1.3M to ~0.9M after the Feb 2034 warning letters forced rebranding to 'craving support'. Some subscribers moved onto AUD- or gambling-coded prescriptions.
interior_life.framing: A side effect, like SSRI sexual dysfunction: named in the label, asked about at refill, adjusted by dose. Platforms may no longer sell it as a feature. HR language moved from 'steadiness' to 'adherence'. Unmuted still calls it sedation, but most users have stopped thinking about it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~11.5M employees are in conditional tracks with clinic or app verification. Lapses cost up to 30% of premium and, in some logistics and call-centre firms, informal standing. The Metabolic Readiness Program ties service members' weight-control prescriptions to body-composition compliance, and commanders see completion status. FAA guidance (2033) allows pilots on approved incretins after a 3-month stable-dose period. DOT allows commercial drivers on approved products but requires medical-examiner disclosure of AUD and gambling-indication use. The two 2030 EEOC ADA charges were resolved by settlement without findings.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoirs have given way to 'lapse' stories about losing coverage. Sportsbook handle per active account fell again in states that fund gambling-disorder prescriptions from betting-tax problem-gambling funds (New Jersey, Massachusetts). Operators now advertise 'responsible play' partnerships with telehealth. Ambient streaming genres persist, but the marketing segment built on calm-plan users dissolved with the rebrand.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Shot dates still organise calendars. Since the label change, partners raise flatness as a dose question, and clinicians step doses down more readily. Couples' therapists report fewer 'parallel lives' complaints than in 2032 and more conflict over one partner's job-tied track: who is allowed to stop, and when.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The argument moved from calm marketing to supply and conditionality. 'American peptides' is a bipartisan slogan after the tariffs and the DPA designation. The gaming industry and some civil-liberties groups oppose state funding of gambling-disorder prescriptions as 'pathologising leisure', while recovery groups support it. Adherence-premium bills stalled again outside Illinois. 'Sedated electorate' talk faded after the label quantified blunting as uncommon.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine at the FDA and assertive at Commerce and DoD. The FDA approved AUD and gambling-disorder indications, retatrutide 12 mg and bimagrumab, labelled emotional blunting and sent warning letters ending calm marketing. Commerce imposed Section 232 tariffs on imported incretin APIs and finished peptides. Congress acted only through the NDAA. No state banned adherence premiums beyond Illinois.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No civilian mandate. The FY2034 NDAA Metabolic Readiness Program funds TRICARE coverage for active-duty and reserve members, conditioned on body-composition compliance, and expands the Army recruit oral pilot to all services for applicants within 10% of standards. OPM requires FEHB carriers covering weight management (plan year 2034) to do so through adherence-verified tracks. Five state Medicaid programmes condition weight-loss coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper and more formal. Clinic administration records, PBM fills and app logs flow to wellness vendors under consent across ~11.5M track enrollees. Military prescriptions sit in readiness records visible to commanders. Medicaid conditional programmes link fill data to community-engagement reporting. Telehealth mood check-ins are still collected, but the sale of 'focus cohorts' slowed after the warning letters.
state.workforce_or_military: The drug is readiness infrastructure. ~0.21M active-duty and reserve members are enrolled; recruiting commands credit it with ~6–8% more eligible applicants. State police in Texas and Ohio and several large metro departments include incretin tracks in fitness-standard remediation. FAA and DOT have set disclosure rules. Large shift-work employers (air freight, warehousing, call centres) run on-site clinic administration.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Supply is politicised. Section 232 tariffs of 60% apply to imported incretin APIs and finished peptides, with exemptions for firms with US capacity commitments. China answered with export licensing on protected amino acids, synthesis resins and finished peptides. DoD used DPA Title III awards and multi-year supply contracts to make Lilly's Indiana API plants and Amgen's Ohio fill-finish site the domestic champions. US–India talks added incretins to the tariff agenda without agreement. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap narrowed to ~25–35× as Indian prices rose.

events.event: Commerce imposes 60% Section 232 tariffs on imported incretin APIs and finished peptides; Beijing answers within weeks with export licensing on peptide precursors and resins, Indian generic prices rise ~35%, and Novo, Lilly and Amgen say they will hold US prices 'given input uncertainty'

After its postmarketing study finds a ~2-point adjusted excess of anhedonia at maintenance doses, FDA adds emotional blunting class-wide as an uncommon, dose-related adverse reaction; February warning letters end 'calm' and 'focus' claims

FY2034 NDAA creates the Metabolic Readiness Program, putting incretin coverage for service members under TRICARE conditional on body-composition compliance, and funds DPA contracts for domestic peptide API at Lilly and Amgen plants

OPM's FEHB rules for plan year 2034 take effect, covering weight management only through adherence-verified tracks; a Business Group on Health survey finds 29% of employers now cover only that way, and a KFF poll finds 44% of households include a current user
FDA approves a 12 mg maintenance strength of Lilly's retatrutide, filed in February 2033, with ~29% mean weight loss, a DXA requirement for adults 60+ and a $449 cash price

FDA approves oral semaglutide for gambling disorder, 13 months after Novo's March 2033 filing and nine months after its alcohol-use-disorder approval; New Jersey and Massachusetts direct problem-gambling funds to cover it

open_tensions: Coverage now depends on compliance. About 11.5 million workers, five state Medicaid programmes, federal employees and the military get the drug only while the record stays clean. One lapse can turn a lost shift, a pregnancy or an illness into lost coverage and regain, and the NIH cycling cohort will not report for years.

Prices stopped falling because of tariffs and Chinese precursor licensing, and the companies holding prices flat also hold the DPA contracts. Part D spend is near $42B on non-obesity codes alone, while the ~$41B obesity benefit stays closed.

Gambling and alcohol disorders are now treatable with an incretin. 'Compulsion' is being stretched to cover shopping, gaming and sex off-label, and the gaming industry is fighting states that pay for the prescriptions from betting taxes.
Children who started before puberty still show no catch-up growth at 36 months. Normalisation keeps adolescent use rising toward 3.3%, and nobody yet knows final adult height.

prose.headline: One in Four Americans Is On It. In 2034 the Question Is Why You Stopped.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about seventy-three million American adults take an incretin drug, a little over a quarter of the country. That is twenty million more than two years ago. Few people under fifty still find it worth mentioning. What gets noticed now is stopping. A colleague who comes back from leave heavier is asked what happened with her coverage. A life-insurance form asks whether you stopped an incretin and why. Teenagers ask their parents why they aren't on one.

The growth did not come from cheaper drugs. Prices stopped falling in the spring of 2033. That May, Commerce put a 60 percent tariff on imported incretin ingredients and finished peptides. Beijing answered with export licences on the amino-acid precursors and resins that every peptide maker needs. Indian generics got about a third more expensive and harder to mail. Novo, Lilly and Amgen said input costs were uncertain and stopped cutting prices. The starting pill is still $149 in the government's cash channel. MariTide is still $249. Wegovy's $1,349 list price is still printed on the box.

The growth came through conditions. Employers did not keep dropping coverage. Most of them made it conditional. Fewer than a quarter cover the drugs on ordinary terms, and nearly three in ten cover them only through monitored tracks. In those tracks a nurse at the warehouse or the air-freight hub gives the monthly shot, and the record decides the premium. Eleven and a half million workers sit in such programmes, and federal employees joined them in January. Five state Medicaid programmes tie coverage to adherence and weight progress. The Pentagon now treats the drug as readiness. The defense bill signed in December 2033 pays for incretins for service members who stay within body-composition standards, opens the recruit pill programme to every service, and funds domestic peptide plants in Indiana and Ohio as a strategic supply. Recruiters say it has widened their pool. Commanders can see who is enrolled.

The other route in runs through addiction. The FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in July 2033 and for gambling disorder in April 2034. Those are not weight-loss uses, so Medicare and Medicaid have to pay for them under the rules they already follow. About a million people on public coverage now take the drug for a craving rather than for their weight. New Jersey and Massachusetts pay for gambling prescriptions out of sports-betting taxes, and the sportsbooks are lobbying against it. Doctors are being asked about shopping, gaming and sex as well.

The drugs got stronger. In March Lilly won approval for a 12-milligram retatrutide dose that takes off nearly three-tenths of body weight. Its label requires a bone scan for older patients and advises resistance training. A muscle-preserving antibody approved last autumn is available for those whose plans will pay.

The flatness has a name now, and it is a smaller one than before. The FDA's study found that after adjustment the excess of real anhedonia is about two in a hundred at full doses. It found nothing measurable at low doses and found that it fades after stopping. The label now lists it as uncommon. Warning letters ended the calm subscriptions' advertising, and most of their customers stayed under new names. No new harm was found in these two years. The old ones remain: fractures in older users, pancreatic trouble after many years, and children who started young growing more slowly, still with no sign of catching up.

The cyclers' faces that marked Memphis in 2032 are rarer, because the hub clinics replaced the mail-order vials. The people who never got the drug are rural, self-employed or old without the right codes. In 2034 the risk most users worry about is losing the coverage.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tanya Ruiz clocks in at 10:40 p.m. at the Memphis air hub and swipes her badge at the clinic window before the sort. It is the third Thursday. The nurse finds the faded bruise from last month, picks the other side and pushes the MariTide in. 'You're green through March,' she says, and the tablet chimes. Green keeps Tanya's premium at $96 instead of $212.

At the 2 a.m. break, Kelvin from the belt line is eating two honey buns. Somebody asks him, not unkindly, whether he got dropped. He says his wife's pregnant and he's off in solidarity. Nobody believes him and nobody pushes.

She drives home at seven with the radio off. Her brother Marcus is on the porch with his phone face-down on the step, which still surprises her. TennCare approved his pill in June under the gambling code. It is the same semaglutide he used to buy as vials off Telegram before the tariff doubled the price. He says the games feel like weather now, there but not his. He says some days the barbecue tastes like weather too. The pharmacist told him that can happen and to say so if it lasts.

Her son DeShawn, fifteen and big like his father was, is at the kitchen table filling out the Army's early-interest form on his phone. There is a box: Willing to enrol in Metabolic Readiness. He has already checked it.

Tanya makes eggs, eats one and puts the plate in the fridge. She sets an alarm for the thirteenth, the date the app's check-in opens.
